Introduction

Hello Lovey Bunny!

Have you ever considered the fact that you were born with an exquisitely designed and arranged brain and mind that is capable of many different layers of consciousness: dreaming, protecting, analyzing, imitating, loving, remembering, hiding, revealing and healing, etc. etc.?

Instead of learning how to integrate all of these different layers, you were taught (and/or you learned on your own) how to push, repress or supress your emotions, to pretend to be confident, to follow or defy authority, and so on and so forth. It is no wonder that you have many different "programs" running in your mind, including child mind, guard, body mind, intuitive mind, fantasy mind, etc.

I learned hypnosis from a lot of people who tried to act as if the subconscious mind worked like a machine, and all they had to do was feed in a command and the machine would do what they put in. For me, a much more useful model was to learn to talk to different parts of myself until they all could listen together.

This guide teaches a method of self-hypnosis to bring the audience of the conscious mind, subconscious mind, body, inner child, protector parts, the adult self, and the Higher Self all into the same room to be able to listen and talk together.

Where do I start? Easy. Just listen, warm up to, protect, clarify, reality test and act on it!

It doesn’t have to be a dramatic trance experience but it does have to lead to a more trustworthy relationship between all parts of the mind.

Let’s call it communion. The conscious mind doesn’t have to shout it’s message from the roof top and the subconscious doesn’t have to rely on symptoms, dreams, cravings, day dreams, and other weird body signals to communicate.

I work with the premise that the subconscious is an ecology, and we must be skilled enough to communicate with its many parts, to separate ourselves into those parts if necessary to better understand them, to heal inner child trauma by reparenting those parts, to coalesce that ecology into a Higher Self or universal heart when need be, and more. I also pull in elements from prompt engineering, and teach literacy in the domain of influence, since hypnosis is far from the only thing that’s hypnotizing us.

Appendix C: The extended de-hypnosis checklist

Use this checklist when any person, ad, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic attraction, or voice inside of yourself tries to exert influence over…

Ask yourself: If this is really true, will it still be there when I’m questioning it? If this is really love, will it still be there when I put healthy boundaries? If this is really guidance, will it still be there when I’ve slept on it? If this is really meant for me, will it still be there when I accept that I’m an adult now?

Before acting, also ask yourself: Is there a sense of urgency here? A sense of secrecy? A sense of shame? A threat of being left out? A promise of specialness? A sexual charge?

Are some people being put forward as spiritually superior?

Is there a demand that something be given up – money, sex, loyalty, silence, obedience?

Is there a narrowing of choices for yourself?

Is any questioning considered a betrayal?

Is there a way of making resistance seem pathological?

Is there a down-grading of ordinary life?

Is there a seduction, or scaring or rescuing of the child in?

Can the adult in still say “no” ?

If you found yourself saying yes to any of these, several in fact, then maybe it’s time to stop going deeper, and to make irreversible decisions until you can get back into the room, in your body, connected to food, sleep, time, and good counsel.

And by the way, a good guide increases your adult self; a bad one replaces it. A good guide can tolerate your “no”; a bad one will reframe it as resistance or ego or fear or low vibration or past trauma or sin, or just more evidence of the need for more guidance.

Hypnosis-specific audit

Did somebody not tell, plainly, that induction mechanics would be used?

Is at least one answer likely to get someone pausing, modding, full on, or stoping?

Does it imply that not noticing it was a secret proof that it worked?

Did it use roles, ownership, obedience, age, identity, or belong-ness, to get an adult to not use their judgement?

Do they tell first, rather than sneak in fractionation, cues, later behavior or memory effects?

Are they exploiting body sensations?

Do they carefully restore all aspects of identity, movement, orientation and critical ability and tell explicitly the session is over when coming out?

If in doubt on any of these, come fully out of it, ask to see a copy of the script, change to a different method, or stop altogether.

Appendix D: Anxiety — body first

Remember that the anxiety is coming from a part of yourself that is a Protector who believes they are trying to save yourself from something bad happening. Maybe they are trying to protect yourself from danger, shame, abandonment, failure, exposure, illness, rejection, losing control, or something that the protector believes will be unbearable for yourself. Rather than getting into a dialogue where it feels as though yourself is interrogating the protector, start with yourself by taking care of the body.

Always work with yourself by taking care of the body first, then the inner child, then doing some inner inquiry work, and then taking some kind of action.

Inner child love

One of the things that can help is putting your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexis and say lovingly, “You are a little one. You are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. Let the adult take this.”

Don’t say the words, just hoping that they will work on your subconscious mind. Say them to yourself like you are talking to a little child that you love.

Reduced breathing / Buteyko-style breathing

NOTE: There are some good things to be said for slowing down the breathing, especially for overbreathers and those subject to panic. Some of this is based on the Buteyko approach. However, it should not be forced, and creating air hunger can increase anxiety for a short period. Take things slowly.

Try breathing through the nose. Try small inhales. Try quiet exhales. Try pausing if it is comfortable. See if it is possible to quiet the breathing. STOP if this creates dizziness, strain, a sense of panic or any other medical concerns.

EFT tapping

One of the simplest aspects of EFT is that it’s something you can do in your body. If you’re worried about something, you can name it, tap on your body, and get in touch with the feeling. There isn’t a ton of evidence, but a 2025 systematic review of EFT and anxiety disorders found seven randomized control trials and noted that EFT was more effective than no intervention in several studies. While it should be handled with a bit of caution, it’s something to keep in mind if you’re not responding to first-line therapies.

Even though I have this anxiety, I am willing to be kind to myself.

Somatic Experiencing

Would it be helpful for to know more or even experience a free intro session to how I work as a Somatic Guide?

It's not about thrusting into the trauma, in SE we learn to track.

The work might begin by tracking and discovering "Where is that activation", and "Where is a neutral place", and then "Where can we move, at a snail's pace, from one to the other?"

Gendlin Focusing

Do all of these with the felt sense of the whole:

Give it time to get one vague sense of the whole. Then, ask:

“What would this like me to know?” etc.

Try out a word or phrase to see if it fits, but also look at what it says about the situation. A word that feels ok might say something that doesn’t fit. It’s good to use both to correct each other.

Body supports

Sometimes the mind is too activated to let meditation to take care of it. It may be useful to start from the body instead. Consider massage, either self or given by someone else, as the first resort. Maybe massage the top of one foot with the other, or the scalp, or a temple, or the back of the neck, or the top of a shoulder, or whatever feels good to touch. (Avoid the front of the neck. Avoid injured, numb, bruised, inflamed, recently surgically-operated-on areas, and varicose veins. Stop if it makes the anxiety symptoms or anything else feel bad, whether immediately or later, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) Other body approaches that may help include heat, pressure, weighted blanket, darkness, favorite calming music, massage gun, etc.

Others mentioned warmth, darkness, favorite music, massage, weighted blanket, breathwork, favorite object, and favorite personal technology.

See my ZHoly3O page for more on the use of ozonated charcoal, “holy water” as an important tool in the protocol of relaxing. Use of Blushield is also detailed there, and may be of some benefit, although not at all essential. The important thing is to get the body to a state of stabilization where one can begin to discern between valid and non-valid messages from the “inner realm”. Once reality tested, take appropriate actions to restore oneself to a grounded state.

Anxiety script

Where is my body? What are my feet doing? What is my butt doing? How am I sitting in the chair? How am I breathing? What is my body doing in this room?

And if you can hear me, little one, know that I am here and that I am here to protect you. Thank you, protector, for alerting me. You do not need to scream. I got the message.

Now if there is something my body needs to do, show me what the first step is for my body to do right now. And if there is nothing my body can do right now, help my body stand down.

I won’t abandon you, but I won’t worship you either.

Troubleshooting

Nothing happens

Start smaller:

“Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”

It feels fake

What is it that feels fake? The words, an image, an expectation, a role? Be clear that not experiencing the inner voice/image is not a resistance or lack of adult capacity. If something is inviting you to do something you explicitly don’t want to do, correct it. It may also be a part that is protecting you, if so talk to it:

“What are you protecting me from?” or “Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?” or “Are you afraid this will just be a performance?”

It could be an inner voice of a parent you are picking up that is enforcing a rule about how you should be to belong, if so don’t argue with it, find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding evidence to strengthen your new adult voice.

It may be that an adult capacity you need is not yet available to you, in that case stop trying to make yourself have an inner voice that you believe and if you have enough observing ego, borrow the capacity you need from someone (real or imagined) who has it. Try out a sentence or action etc and see how it goes.

The subconscious will not answer

There may not be an answer. There may not be a helpful answer. It may be that this isn’t a helpful question to ask at all, and you need to try a different one, or rest, or finish. But if you do sense that there’s something you need to consider about trust, what if you asked:

“What would you need to know in order to trust me?”

You might be surprised by how profoundly un-mystical the answer is. “I need to know you’ll set a boundary.” “I need to know you’ll follow through.” “I need to know you’ll stop leaving.” “I need to know you’ll stop telling me that what I’m asking for isn’t actually what I need.”

The inner child will not appear

If you can discern who the guard is, talk to it. If you can’t, then simply talk in terms of your feelings or preferences.

“Even if you don’t let me in, there are things I can do to help you feel safer.”

Even if there isn’t a clear child state to talk to, you can still build identity and do reparenting by working with whatever you are aware of–preferences, curiosity, or even a statement that you’re new to this and would like to try something and see how it goes.

You get anxious

Figure out whether your anxiety is manageable and you want to allow it to continue or whether you need to do something to reduce it. If it’s escalating or overwhelming, stop whatever you’re doing to help your body first.

Where are your feet? Your chair? Focus on your breath. Be with your body in the room.

Talk to your Little and Protector parts: “Little one, I’m here for you. Protector, I know you’re trying to protect me. Thank you for letting me know. Do you need me to do something? If so, what? If not, can you let my body know it can stand down?”

If your anxiety is causing you to have chest pain, faint, have suicidal thoughts, become psychotic or manic, severely dissociate, not sleep, or makes you want to hurt yourself or someone else, get help from a professional. For a longer list of ways to work with anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.

You dissociate or feel unreal

This is the time for you to open your eyes, to start moving again, to start touching the textured world again. Name the five things you can see. Your practice for today is over.

You become grandiose

Eat, sleep, work your chores, be humble again

Mantra: “Will this insight survive sleeping and eating and time, humility and feedback?

You become too analytical

Three things to remember when the practice starts to turn into a performance:

1. Stop trying to make it better. Put one hand on the heart, the other on the solar plexis, and say to yourself,

2. “I am not here to do this perfectly. I am here to be in relationship with that which is deeper than the surface of my mind.”

3. “What can I do to make this more a communion than a performance?”

4. Sometimes the answer to that question is to be quiet, sometimes it is to rest, sometimes it is to do something. Do whatever the answer is that comes to yourself.

You become too blissful or diffuse

Have it ask you to be specific about the bliss

“What can you do to be loving right now?”

You want the hidden truth immediately

Do n't pry

“Ask it to show you the next capacity instead of the next content.”

You keep daydreaming

Sit up and open your eyes

“What real action is this fantasy replacing?”

You get stuck in spiritual bypass

“What part of this situation have you not yet allowed the descent of divine love to pour into this wound?”

Sometimes when you are opening in a certain way and you are expecting love or freedom to come, it’s revealing to yourself the next level of depth that you are capable of opening to. But you can’t command it to come for the child. Sometimes when you try prayer, it reveals what abandonment or condemnation it evokes for you. Sometimes it’s good to see how a certain kind of teacher has betrayed you and how you were damaged, and that’s something you need to question. It’s not going to be helped by more of the same.

Sometimes you need practical help and you don’t see enough of a life horizon to help you. “What direction would the Leader choose now?”

“What would prove to the inner child that the adult is real?”

Then do the thing.

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

You don’t have to know the terms to use the system. If you want to brush up on the art of imagery, how imagery is linked to bodily states, how to effectively rehearse new behaviors, how to choose more effective sentences to say to yourself, etc., then you might want to read this appendix. If you don’t know a little bit about NLP, it’s easy to turn NLP into a bag of tricks and forget that love, truth, contact, and consent are essential.

The four NLP layers

When it works, it works on a Sensory Level of NLP: changing where people see or hear an image, the distance or size or brightness, the volume of a sound, the posture of a remembered person, the pressure of an unpleasant sensation.

Second, it works on a State Level of NLP: helping them to access warmth, or a feeling of adult-ness, or courage, or steadiness, or love, or clarity.

Third, it works on a Strategy level of NLP: helping people to practice a new strategy.

Fourth, it works on a Language Level of NLP: pacing what is there, opening up people’s awareness, presuming their ability to do something safe, linking cause and effect in new ways, embedding suggestions, or asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative, or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

It's called the Milton Model and has to do with the architecture of the sentence. When I say "Relax now", or "Stop being anxious", or even "Trust me" a part of me braces against it.

The idea is to use indirect language to get past the part that wants to argue with me, and get to the place I want to go to.

To do that, I start with something I know to be true, and I take the pressure off by presuming the least possible capacity in the person and invite just one movement:

"As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone."

That way I pace reality, I open up awareness, I validate the function of what I'm doing, I presuppose the capacity to do what I want, I use a bridge to make the link easier, I invite only one small movement, and I have a way of testing with the body if it's happening.

Pattern 1: Pacing and leading — truth before suggestion

What is it looks like to pace and lead?

Here is an example of pacing and leading for anxiety:

It can be as simple as: Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite etc.

“It is completely true that the sensation of _______ (or emotion of _____) is coming up for me right now. It makes complete sense that a part of me is trying to protect me by doing/thinking ________. While that is completely true, another completely true thing is that there is a part of me that is adult, and that is breathing in this room right now, and is willing to listen.

Pattern 2: Awareness verbs

Awareness Verbs: Notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider, etc.

Pattern 3: Presuppositions

Caution: The powerful technique of presupposition (embedding a statement as if it were true) is best used in the positive key of assuming choice, when it will occur, ability, not doing something unsafe, love, being adult, etc. Never use presupposition to imply that the other person must obey.

Be careful with how language link events. Words like “as, while, because, when, after, before, which means” etc are all words that can be used to link events.

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

The Milton Model opens things up. The Meta Model asks for clarification. To be ethical, one needs to use both.

How specifically? According to whom? Compared to what? Always? Never? What exactly would happen? How do I know? What evidence would change my mind?

Use the Milton Model to soften into the body. Use the Meta Model to get back to the truth.

Sensory, state, and strategy tools

Submodalities — editing the form, not denying the truth

Are there sensory qualities to the fear, craving, fantasy, belief, or memory? Is it close or far? Bright or dim? Loud or quiet? Moving or static? Heavy or light? Somewhere in your body or outside? If you notice any of these sensory qualities, you can work with them. If not, skip this tool.

What if you changed the sensory qualities?

“It would not be cenzorship to change the sensory qualities. It would only be a way for me to stay in contact with you.”

Ask your guard if it’s ok to change the sensory qualities. For example, you might say:

“Would it be ok if I moved the image back a couple of inches? Or turned down the volume a notch? This would enable me to hear you better with my adult mind.”

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

An anchor is a cue that triggers a state. It can be anything - putting your hand on your heart, touching two fingers together, taking a breath, saying a word, a particular posture, scent, song, and so on. Choose something, then find a real state to anchor it to. When you're clearly in the state, apply the anchor and say, 'This is available' . (If you're using the anchor to get back into hypnosis, find a nice useful state - you don't need to be at the peak of emotion, just in a nice receptive state. For more about that, see 'A shortcut back into hypnosis' in the main induction section. ) Make sure you also have a way to bring yourself back to a nice, calming, alert state when you want to be fully awake (see 'synchronicity' above for a way of doing that).

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Sometimes when my clients notice a synchronicity they are asking straight way what it means. Sometimes it does give them a very good insight, sometimes it gives them a reason to start obsessing and look for patterns in everything. I am using noticing a synchronicity in a different way. I am using it as a signal to WAKE UP.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice a synchronicity, I use it to wake up in whatever state I am in at that moment, feel my body, the room I am in and go to the highest state I can where I can objectively and clearly see the situation I am in from the highest possible perspective, feeling my body and being still within the human reality. From this place I feel whatever feelings, search for the truth of the situation, and if I am in a negative state, I check if there is a message of my Inner Child, Protector, if I need to go through some grieving, if there is a message of my physical body about some problem that needs solving, or if there is a need for me to take some action in this situation. From this place of clarity and peace I am free to choose what to do next and usually I can do at least one thing that comes from a loving place. In this state I am also free and joyful and I feel grateful.

In short it is my cue to: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

It enables me to not get into identification, but still hear the message of the state if it is a negative one.

Installing the synchronicity cue

Mentally rehearse: when next synchronicity noticed (even harmless ones count),

feel 'whoa' as attention stimulated,

feel feet/body/breath/room to stimulate re-embodiment,

reiterate to yourself "when I notice synchronicity, it is a bell to wake me up, not a message to heed",

optionally ask Nurturer/Protector/Leader their thoughts,

rehearse further steps to get a more grounded and wide view,

rehearse what additional action to take, and finally rehearse waking completely,

Mind the caveats : it must be self-authored, obviously under control, reversible, and restricted to just helping orientation. It must not be used for decision-making, intuition, inhibition, or otherwise be under someone else's control.

This is a kind of implementation intention , for which there is evidence of efficacy (a good starting point is this paper by Gollwitzer ). Note that this specific application of implementation intentions probably hasn't been studied.

Synchronicity cues, like any cue, run the risk of creating false positives because you are creating an association in your mind by rehearsing it (this is the same mechanism by which synchronicity cues work), and when you are absorbed and/or destabilized, your mind may look for that pattern and interpret it as present when it may not actually be. Research has shown that people that score highly on apophenia (the tendency to perceive meaningful patterns where none exists) also score highly on false positives for patterns that are not present, and also score highly on traits on the psychosis spectrum (Blain et al., Grant et al.).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are creating false positives (you find yourself compelled to scan your environment for them, you are unable to sleep, you are anxious, you feel that random events are occurring to communicate something to you specifically, you find yourself unable to tell if they are real or not, etc.), you should deactivate them.

You can do this by simply ceasing to rehearse them, and saying, while fully awake, “Synchronicity is no longer to be used as a cue, and I let it go.” Also remove it from your list of cues so that you stop rehearsing it.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

When I reframe something that is dishonest with myself in the process, I’m no better off than before, so I have to be honest when I reframe. To reframe in a helpful way is to ask myself a series of questions like: “What else could be true here?” or “What is this part trying to do for me?” or “How would my Nurturer reframe this?” or “How would my Protector reframe this?” or “How would my Leader reframe this?” and so on.

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

1. How do I feel about this from inside myself? 2. If I were inside of this other person (or tree, or dog or whatever is not-you), how might I feel? 3. If I were across the room watching this, what would I see? 4. From the universal heart, what might be true, loving, clear about boundaries, and good for everyone involved?

Yes, it’s possible to use these positions to let yourself off the hook. It’s also possible to use them to get off the hook! Use them to see the truth from more than one angle. They’re a great way to get out of a prison of perception.

Future pacing — let the future test the insight

Don’t end with “I understand.” Ask where life will test the understanding, picture the actual cue, and rehearse the smallest better response.

“If [cue], then I [small action].”

The Swish, softened

In classic NLP, one of the uses of the Swish was to replace an old image of yourself with a new, better one. Some people find that method jarring. So here is a gentler way to do it, leaving the old pattern in place, but letting it sit side by side with a new pattern, so that the client can feel, in their body, which one they want to pursue, and see what it would take to get there.

Parts integration, without pretending the conflict is solved

“What does one side want?” “What does the other side fear?” “What need sits under both?” “What third option honors both without letting either run the whole life?”

To “explain away” a true signal that is coming through

To override any fear signals that are present

To bring up memories, or to manipulate others

To create a false urgency within someone, when they need time

Running the whole NLP sequence

Induce or contain (if client already in altered state).

Ask permission to work with this part.
